PullRequest.Title: agentHost: use SDK metadata for native customization discovery
PullRequest.Body:

Use the SDK's definition URIs, opaque plugin ownership IDs, and resolved installation roots for native customization discovery.

- Remove ancestor-manifest searches and native plugin directory rescanning used to reconstruct hook/MCP ownership.
- Expose readable hook definitions when supplied by the SDK, while keeping fileless hooks non-readable.
- Keep SDK-enumerated hooks as individual actions without re-expanding readable definition files, preserving stable IDs, per-action enablement, and source navigation.
- Preserve standard MCP App capabilities on native plugin MCP children.
- Join native contributions by complete plugin ID. Native plugin names and child listings now reflect SDK inventory rather than filesystem-inferred additions.
- Preserve standalone contributions when inventory lookup fails, and retain the existing standalone workspace-hook discovery workaround.
- Update discovery, provider-integration, and E2E coverage.

Related: #335500.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each customization discovery refresh repeated filesystem manifest probes for every native plugin contribution and then rescanned all five component classes for each deduplicated plugin root, even though the SDK had already enumerated the effective contributions.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Customization publication and refresh latency, plus filesystem I/O, scaled with both the number/depth of plugin contribution paths and the number and size of installed plugin trees.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed toPluginCustomizations implementation resolves roots from one SDK plugin inventory and projects only SDK-enumerated children, eliminating per-contribution ancestor manifest searches and per-plugin full directory parsing from each discovery refresh.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, every settled SessionCustomizationDiscovery refresh collected each SDK-reported plugin contribution in pluginFiles, then line 749 called findPluginRoot for every distinct contribution URI. findPluginRoot walked parent directories and hasPluginManifest probed up to five manifest locations at each level. After roots were deduplicated, the same refresh called parsePlugin for every root; parsePlugin reads the manifest and scans hooks, MCP, skills, agents, and instructions. SessionDiscoveredEntry runs this discovery on the session-creation getCustomizationsSettled critical path and on debounced watcher/plugin refreshes. The changed implementation instead gathers opaque plugin IDs, makes one conditional SDK plugins.list inventory request, and joins the already-discovered children in memory without ancestor probes or component-directory rescans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial/session customization discovery before publishing a new session snapshot
Scenarios.CriticalPath: getCustomizationsSettled and getAppliedCustomizations await the per-anchor SessionDiscoveredEntry discovery. Agent, rule, skill, hook, and MCP SDK discovery plus watcher resolution run in parallel; the new plugin inventory lookup runs afterward only when at least one discovered child has a plugin ID, so it is on the critical path in native-plugin sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the SDK global plugin inventory to map opaque plugin IDs to resolved roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero calls when no discovered contribution has a plugin ID; otherwise exactly one call per settled anchor discovery, independent of plugin/contribution count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No plugins.list call occurred here. Instead, every distinct plugin contribution URI triggered an ancestor walk with multiple filesystem manifest probes, then every deduplicated plugin root was fully parsed and its hooks, MCP, skills, agents, and rules directories scanned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequentially follows the parallel SDK discovery phase and must complete before native plugin containers can be published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse SDK-enumerated agent and skill definition files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One agent parse per discovered non-builtin agent as before; one skill parse per discovered non-builtin skill. Plugin skills are newly parsed here but replace whole-plugin scanning of every skill directory and undiscovered entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents were already parsed individually and then plugin roots were parsed again. Plugin skills were skipped individually but read during the later whole-plugin parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Agent reads are serialized by the loop; skill reads run concurrently and both must finish before inventory joining.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve discovery directories and maintain filesystem watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched resolveAll per discovery refresh for cached discovery paths and their ancestors; unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same watcher resolution, plus the now-removed plugin ancestor probes and component scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with SDK discovery and completes before publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective scale is one SDK inventory call per active anchor discovery; in-memory joining is O(installed plugins × discovered children). Removed filesystem work scaled with distinct plugin contribution URIs, ancestor depth, plugin count, and plugin tree contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one anchor, five SDK discovery requests and watcher filesystem resolution run concurrently, followed by one plugins.list request. One SessionDiscoveredEntry is shared by chats using the same ordered anchor set. Different active clients/session anchor sets can discover concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directory definitions are cached on the SessionCustomizationDiscovery instance after the cold scan. Plugin inventory is not cached, but is skipped entirely for no-plugin results and is one call per refresh. The anchor shares one discovery instance among chats with identical roots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines, parser implementation, and session critical-path ownership establish both old and new work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK plugins.list latency and typical active-anchor counts are not measured, but the boundary cardinality and replacement of substantially broader filesystem work are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The single conditional inventory call replaces higher-cardinality ancestor probes and full plugin rescans; simple in-memory joins are bounded by realistic plugin inventories.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization refresh after watched file changes or plugin install/enable/disable/uninstall
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Watcher changes queue a 100 ms debounced refresh; plugin operations explicitly await refreshDiscoveredCustomizations before returning. Each started refresh performs discovery and, for native plugin children, one inventory lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh all active customization anchors and request plugin inventory for anchors with native plugin children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one plugins.list per active discovered anchor for each explicit global refresh; watcher bursts are debounced per anchor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-anchor fan-out performed repeated local filesystem ancestor searches and full plugin parsing instead of plugins.list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit plugin operations await all active-client refreshes; watcher refreshes update publication asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ancestor manifest existence probes and five-class plugin directory scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, manifest probes scaled with every distinct contribution path and ancestor depth, followed by one full scan per plugin root; after the diff, zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Present before the diff and removed here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously blocked every settled refresh and plugin operation awaiting refresh; removed by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active client count, distinct active anchor sets, watched change frequency after debouncing, installed plugin count, and discovered contribution count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per anchor, queued refreshes coalesce through Delayer and an in-flight refresh is canceled when superseded. Explicit plugin refresh fans out concurrently across active clients and each client's active anchors; there is no global limiter, but each anchor performs at most one lookup per settled refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm refreshes reuse discovered-directory metadata but intentionally re-run effective SDK discovery. Debouncing coalesces rapid file events; plugin inventory has no cross-anchor cache, while each anchor is shared among chats with the same roots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for refresh coalescing, fan-out, and boundary counts based on SessionDiscoveredEntry and PluginController call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-client/multi-anchor populations are possible but prevalence is unknown. The new concurrent inventory fan-out replaces more expensive per-anchor scans, so it does not establish a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff does not increase effective expensive work relative to the prior refresh path and materially removes repeated filesystem I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or refreshing the AI customization hook list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The items model fetches provider items through a cached promise, then hook normalization may read hook definition files before rendering. SDK-enumerated hook actions now bypass file expansion even when their definition URI is readable; ordinary hook-file records still expand.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse ordinary hook files into individual list actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per ordinary readable hook-file item per hook-list fetch; zero reads for SDK-enumerated actions marked isHookAction, including multiple actions sharing one definition URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every readable hook item was treated as a hook file and read/expanded. SDK actions previously used non-readable discovery URIs, so they also avoided reads; the marker preserves that behavior while allowing navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ordinary file expansion must complete before hook list items are returned; SDK action reads are removed from this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of ordinary hook files and SDK-enumerated actions, including multiple actions sharing one definition file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observed sections can refetch concurrently, but ItemProviderItemSource coalesces provider retrieval through cachedPromise. expandHookFileItems processes ordinary hook files sequentially; SDK action items take the no-read branch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider customizations are cached until provider/skill changes. Expanded normalized hook results are recomputed per section fetch, but the diff prevents the newly readable SDK action URIs from causing file reads or duplicate expansion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added isHookAction branch and tests directly establish zero reads for readable SDK actions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical hook counts are small and no new expensive operation remains on the SDK-action path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The marker specifically prevents new filesystem reads and parsing that readable SDK definition URIs would otherwise trigger.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The production change replaces repeated per-contribution manifest searches and whole-plugin rescans with one conditional SDK inventory call and bounded in-memory joining; UI hook mapping preserves the prior no-read behavior for SDK actions. Recorded the removed repeated-I/O path as a concrete regression fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
